items: Every night is now its own session — starting a new one no longer wipes the last, and old setlists stay around to revisit.
The app opens on the club's session history — go back to a past night or start a new one.
The app is now called Setlister — the whiteboard of wishes is the board you snap.
Sessions are named by their date automatically, in your own language and format.
These very notes — new features are announced right here from now on.
The What's new link at the bottom of the session list now shows the full history, not just the newest entry.
Copy or download the setlist straight from the “Up next” heading — no more digging through settings.
Settings now opens on your name and the songbook; the parser knobs are tucked under “Advanced”.
See who's here: shared sessions show everyone currently connected.
Played songs collapse into a one-line count above Up next.
The Bin now lives inside Requests as a collapsed group.
Swipe a song sideways to move it between Up next and Requests.
Share a session: everyone with the link sees the same lists, live.
Set your name in settings — songs show who added them.
Swipe right to mark a song played, swipe left to bin it.
Requests and Up next are separate lists — promote what you'll actually play.
Type-ahead songbook search when adding a request by name.
First version: snap the request whiteboard and get a songbook-matched setlist.
